title: Comments Deodorizing Block Length
pattern: Inline comments placed above large, complex conditional blocks explaining what the block checks or executes.
why_bad: Comments as deodorant for bad code. If a block needs a sentence to explain its intent, it should be extracted into a separate, well-named function. Keeping it inline forces readers to parse complex boolean logic rather than reading a high-level descriptor.
detection: Inline comment preceding a block of code (more than 5 lines) or complex conditional statements, where the comment explains the high-level intent of that specific block.
counterexample: The condition extracted into a named predicate (`is_eligible_for_senior_discount`) whose call site reads as prose without any comment.
fix: Extract the block or condition into a helper function named after the comment's intent.
source: Martin Fowler, *Refactoring* (2018), Chapter 3 ("Bad Smells in Code - Comments").
